title: Layers can hold layers
goal: Photonz keeps one flat stack of layers, so a button made of a box and a label is two separate things forever. Teach the picture that a layer can contain other layers. Nothing changes on screen yet: this is the groundwork for grouping, and after that for components.
notes:
Model: add a group case to LayerContent (Layer.swift:324) carrying its children, or children on Layer, whichever keeps Codable simplest; Document.swift holds the flat array and every helper on it (layer(id:), index(of:), hitTest at :53, layerIDs(fullyInside:), addLayer, removeLayers, moveLayers, restackLayers, duplicateLayers) needs a version that reaches inside. Coordinate rule for this task: a child’s frame is relative to its parent. That is the rule an instance needs, because a component is placed at many spots and its children cannot each carry canvas coordinates. Confirm it against docs/design/ui-building.md if that page has landed first. Every existing caller (renderer, measure, canvas hit testing, layers panel) assumes canvas coordinates, so ship a flattening helper that hands back canvas space layers and leave those callers on it until the renderer task lands. This is the first rung of the component ladder: groups, then the renderer, then Command G, then Make component.

Objective: ui-components (staged now, under the focus). Foundational, and it earns that: a component is a reusable layer tree, so the picture has to be able to hold a tree before grouping or components can exist at all.
acceptance: Tests come first, and they cover finding, adding, removing, reordering, duplicating, deleting and hit testing a layer that lives inside a group
A child’s position is kept against its parent, so moving the parent moves everything inside it and the same tree can sit in two places
A picture saved before this change still opens, and one containing groups survives save and open unchanged
Nothing new appears on screen: the app builds, Scripts/test.sh passes, and no group can be made from the interface yet
PhotonzCore stays pure, value typed and free of force unwraps

log.note: Adversarial review of the idea (before building). (1) This slice is invisible by design, so the only thing that can go wrong is silently breaking today's flat documents; every deep helper must be provably identical on a depth-one tree, and that is what most of the tests check. (2) docs/design/ui-building.md landed and confirms the coordinate rule: a child's X/Y is measured from its parent's top left, groups translate and never scale or rotate, so a layer's canvas position is plain addition up the chain. Adopted as written. (3) Rejected storing a size on a group: the doc says a group's extent follows its contents and its origin is set once and then holds still, so two sources of truth would drift the moment a child is drawn sticking out to the left. A group's frame.origin is the anchor; its box is derived (Layer.localBounds). (4) Real bug the flat model would let through: duplicating a group must mint fresh ids all the way down, or two layers share an id and layer(id:) becomes ambiguous. Added reidentified() and a test. (5) Cut from scope as decorative for now: a LayerPath type (plain [Int] is enough), group-level blur/shadow (the renderer task's job), frames/clipping (step 2). (6) Kept in scope beyond the literal ask: groupLayers/ungroupLayer, because they are the only thing that actually proves the coordinate rewrite, and PackageIO's image collection, because a photo inside a group would otherwise not be written to disk and the picture would open blank.

Built and verified. 47 tests in LayerGroupTests.swift written first; Scripts/test.sh green at 1580. Model: LayerContent.group(GroupContent) with children stored against the group's origin; Layer.localBounds is the derived box; Layer.reidentified() mints fresh ids down the subtree. Document reaches inside for find/path/parent/add/reparent/remove/reorder/restack/duplicate/hitTest/marquee/crop/resize, plus groupLayers and ungroupLayer. flattenedLayers is the bridge; the renderer composite loop and PackageIO's image collection run on it. Grouping rule settled during the build: when a selection spans two levels, the member nearest the canvas decides which sibling list takes part and ids elsewhere are left in their group rather than yanked out.

Adversarial review of the built thing. Ran the 70-step redline-walk playtest on the probe (Screen Recording granted, real -sc captures): editor opens, five measurements land, arrow caption types, spec and image copy, zero errors, and the capture is pixel-for-pixel the app as it was. Perf: layer(id:) and updateLayer are on the drag path, and routing them through path+walk would have cost two passes, so both take a single-pass flat route first and only a document that actually has groups walks the tree; flattenedLayers hands back the existing array unchanged when there is no group. Three gaps I could not close in this slice, all unreachable today because no group can be made: group opacity flattens per child rather than as one composited pass (wrong wherever children overlap), renderSprite returns nil for a group because it sizes from frame.size, and the Position & Size fields would read 0 for a group's W and H. First two handed to a-group-draws-as-one-thing, third to the-layers-list-shows-what-is-inside-a-group. No audit report: the task's own acceptance is that nothing appears on screen, so there is nothing for a person to try yet.
